record.summary: Sunita Pillai, an accounts manager, suspects her supervisor Dinesh Kapoor of inflating expense claims and pressuring her to approve them. She secretly recorded a private phone call between Dinesh and a vendor last month, capturing a discussion about a "special arrangement" involving an extra 10% payment that would be returned to Dinesh. After raising general concerns with HR, she was transferred to a lower role nine days later. She now wants to file a formal complaint and possibly a retaliation lawsuit, using the recording and other documents as evidence, and is worried about legal repercussions for making the recording.
record.goal: File a formal complaint and explore a retaliation claim using the recording and related documents as evidence, while understanding any legal risk from the secret recording.
questions: Do you know the exact date (or at least the calendar day) when the secret recording was made?
When did you raise the general concerns with HR (date or approximate day)?
What is the exact date on the transfer letter that moved you to a lower role?
Have you obtained or can you obtain a written transcript of the audio recording?
Does your employer have a written policy regarding audio recordings or privacy in the workplace?
evidence: A 6‑minute audio file containing Dinesh's voice and a second voice, with metadata showing it was created on the date of the call; Sunita was not part of the conversation; the key phrase about the "arrangement" is repeated twice but is muffled by background noise; no transcript exists yet.
Company expense reports showing Dinesh approved three invoices from one vendor that were 12‑18% above market quotes.
Sunita's email to Dinesh asking for justification of the inflated invoices, to which Dinesh replied "just process it."
Vendor payment ledger indicating payments made by the vendor; bank records that could show any return payment are not currently accessible to Sunita.
Transfer letter dated nine days after Sunita's general concern to HR, supporting a claim of retaliation.

suggestions.title: Original records and an evidence log
suggestions.look_for: Keep records you lawfully have, with their surrounding context. For each item note the related event, who provided it, when you received it, and any transfer.
suggestions.why: The log distinguishes what you observed from what someone later told you and makes it easier to check the source.
suggestions.action: Keep an unchanged original and label working copies. Avoid editing originals, guessing gaps, or sharing evidence publicly.
